items.question: Can you tell how the exposed and unexposed groups were identified, and did both come from the same source population?
items.why: Groups drawn from different places differ in more than the exposure, so the comparison can end up measuring the gap between two populations instead of the effect of the exposure.

items.question: Does the abstract say how exposure was measured, and was the same method applied to everyone rather than leaving it to what people remembered?
items.why: Exposure captured loosely, or captured differently for different participants, blurs the boundary between the groups and usually drags the estimate toward no difference.

items.question: Were outcomes sought and classified the same way in both groups, ideally by people who did not know each participant's exposure?
items.why: If exposed participants are watched more closely, or judged by someone expecting a result, extra cases surface in that group for reasons unconnected to the exposure.

items.question: Does the abstract name the other factors that could explain the association, and show that the analysis accounted for them?
items.why: Exposed and unexposed people differ in habits, illness and access to care, so an association reported with no adjustment at all is usually explained by those differences.

items.question: Even after adjustment, can you name an important factor that went unmeasured and would push the result in the reported direction?
items.why: Adjustment removes only what was measured, and measuring something poorly removes only part of it, so a modest association can survive as leftover confounding alone.

items.question: Do participants appear to have been observed over a period that matches how long the condition of interest takes to develop?
items.why: A study that stops before the outcome has had time to occur collects few events and wide uncertainty, which can make a real effect look like nothing at all.

items.question: Can you see what share of each group was followed to the end, and whether the people who dropped out differed between the groups?
items.why: People leave a cohort for reasons tied to how they are doing, so heavy or uneven loss bends the result in a direction you cannot work out from the abstract.

items.question: Is it clear that the exposure was already present before the outcome began, rather than being recorded once the condition was developing?
items.why: When exposure is recorded after early disease has set in, the illness may have caused the exposure rather than the reverse, which turns the reported story around.
